title: Stuart Bergen's band, the flatbed truck and loud music
summary: Allen remembers Stuart Bergen's band playing in Audubon Park on a truck; they talk about union concerts and liking loud music.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: because you'd come back i came back in 53 from san francisco where you've done your internship right well i'll just remember that exact date and i had a pretty steady thing well yeah that that's what i was going to say was that uh stuart bergen had found tom brown and harry shields yeah well the stuart said we thought we all thought we were going to be discovered in those days to me recently we're talking about and uh of course stuart wasn't discovered if anybody was discovered would have been tom and harry and uh uh they went on to joe and johnny but we certainly enjoyed stuart's then i can remember going up to audubon park and they were playing on a flatbed truck and what the occasion was i don't know but right there on magazine street i believe yeah right off the street we could hop the bus and get there with no trouble from canal street just hop the magazine bus i guess it was a bus
I suspect that sometimes some of these groups played concerts and parks and stuff sponsored by the Musicians Union or something.

Yeah. Except Stewart wasn't in the union. Oh, that's a good reason. Yeah, and maybe it's why he got the job too. It may have been some sort of benefit or, but I don't, it was one of those things which I can't remember any reason for. I don't remember that being a dance or that he was advertising anything. Did you ever go on an advertising truck? No, I never did.

I've seen them and heard them of course, but I've never been on one. Sounds like it'd be fun, but I guess it would depend on where you sat. Yeah. You know, I've always liked my music loud, but I think sitting with my head in front of the trumpet or trombone might be a little bit wearing after a bit.
But did you, it seemed to me we never minded loudness then.
No, I liked it. Basically, you could tell the people who were really eager, I guess, because they were usually standing around the bandstand. Yeah. And. And. .
